title: Transparent Data Encryption
description: Protect data at rest with Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and manage encryption keys and certificates properly.

blocks.text: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) encrypts the entire database at the page level. When data is written to disk, SQL Server encrypts the page before storing it. When data is read into memory, SQL Server decrypts the page automatically. Applications see no difference, and no application code changes are required. TDE protects against threats like stolen backup tapes or unauthorized disk access.

blocks.title: What TDE Protects
blocks.text: TDE encrypts data files (.mdf, .ndf, .ldf) and backup files. It does not protect data in transit (use TLS for that) and does not encrypt data already held in memory.

TDE relies on a nested key hierarchy. The Database Master Key (DMK) in master protects the Certificate. The Certificate protects the Database Encryption Key (DEK) in the user database. The DEK encrypts and decrypts page data. Backing up every key in this chain is essential for recovery.

data.caption: TDE key hierarchy and encryption flow
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Database Master Key] --> B[Certificate in master]
    B --> C[Database Encryption Key]
    C --> D[Encrypts Database Pages]
    D --> E[Data at Rest on Disk]
    F[Backup Certificate] --> G[Restore on Another Server]
    G --> C
    H[Backup DMK] --> A

blocks.text: To enable TDE, you must first create a master key in master if one does not already exist. Then create a certificate protected by that master key. Finally, create the DEK in the target database and alter the database to set encryption on. The process can take time depending on database size because every page must be read, encrypted, and rewritten.

blocks.title: Enable Transparent Data Encryption
blocks.content: Step-by-step T-SQL to enable TDE on a database.
blocks.code:
USE [master];
GO

-- Step 1: Create a database master key if it does not exist
CREATE MASTER KEY ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'M@st3rK3y!2026';
GO

-- Step 2: Create a certificate to protect the DEK
CREATE CERTIFICATE TDECert
    WITH SUBJECT = 'Certificate for TDE on AppDB';
GO

-- Step 3: Switch to the target database and create the DEK
USE [AppDB];
GO

CREATE DATABASE ENCRYPTION KEY
    WITH ALGORITHM = AES_256
    ENCRYPTION BY SERVER CERTIFICATE TDECert;
GO

-- Step 4: Enable encryption
ALTER DATABASE [AppDB] SET ENCRYPTION ON;
GO

-- Step 5: Verify encryption state
SELECT name, is_encrypted,
       encryption_state,
       encryptor_type,
       percent_complete
FROM sys.dm_database_encryption_keys;
GO

blocks.title: Encryption State Values
blocks.text: encryption_state 0 = No encryption, 1 = Encryption in progress, 2 = Encrypted, 3 = Decryption in progress, 5 = Decryption in progress. Do not take unencrypted backups of a database after encryption begins.

If you lose the certificate or master key, you cannot restore the database on another server. Always back up the certificate and master key immediately after creating them. Store backups in a secure, offsite location with strict access controls.

blocks.title: Backup Certificate and Master Key
blocks.content: Securely export the TDE certificate and master key.
blocks.code:
USE [master];
GO

-- Backup the TDE certificate
BACKUP CERTIFICATE TDECert
    TO FILE = 'C:\Backup\TDECert.cer'
    WITH PRIVATE KEY (
        FILE = 'C:\Backup\TDECertKey.pvk',
        ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'C3rtB@ckup!2026'
    );
GO

-- Backup the master key
BACKUP MASTER KEY
    TO FILE = 'C:\Backup\MasterKey.key'
    ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'M@st3rK3yB@ckup!2026';
GO

blocks.text: Restoring an encrypted database to another server requires the same certificate and master key. Restore the master key first, then restore the certificate. Once the certificate exists on the destination server, the backup restore proceeds normally.

blocks.title: Restore Certificate on Destination Server
blocks.content: Prepare a new server to restore an encrypted database backup.
blocks.code:
USE [master];
GO

-- Restore the master key
RESTORE MASTER KEY
    FROM FILE = 'C:\Backup\MasterKey.key'
    DECRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'M@st3rK3yB@ckup!2026'
    ENCRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'N3wM@st3rK3y!2026';
GO

-- Restore the certificate
CREATE CERTIFICATE TDECert
    FROM FILE = 'C:\Backup\TDECert.cer'
    WITH PRIVATE KEY (
        FILE = 'C:\Backup\TDECertKey.pvk',
        DECRYPTION BY PASSWORD = 'C3rtB@ckup!2026'
    );
GO

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
points: TDE encrypts data files and backups transparently with no application changes.
The key hierarchy is DMK → Certificate → DEK.
Always back up the certificate and master key, or the database is unrecoverable on another server.
TDE protects data at rest but does not protect data in transit or in memory.
blocks.takeaway: Enable TDE, back up the keys immediately, and test the restore process before you need it in production.
